children: Flex is buying EPC Power in a $4.4 billion deal, and plans to include the company in the upcoming spin off of its cloud and power infrastructure segment.

EPC Power provides power conversion solutions for data center and grid applications, which Flex anticipates will help it capitalize on growing AI infrastructure demand, and the shift to next generation data center power architectures.

"A generational shift in power architecture is underway, driven by rising power density and the changing demands of digital infrastructure," said Revathi Advaithi, Chief Executive Officer of Flex. He added that along with Flex's existing power, cooling and compute capabilities, adding EPC power expands it ability to design and deliver digital infrastructure as an integrated product.
EPC is currently on pace to generate about $800 million of revenue this year, with organic revenue growth of 40% expected next year.

The acquisition is expected to boost the growth and margin profile of Flex's cloud and power infrastructure segment. In May, Flex said it planned to separate that business into a new publicly traded company.
Flex is evaluating various financing alternatives and expects to fund the deal with a combination of debt and equity.
The deal is expected to close by the end of 2026, and the spin off is due to occur in the first quarter of 2027.
